operations.name: subscription.cancel
operations.description: End a subscription when its current paid period (or trial) ends: nothing more is charged, and what it gives lasts until then. A signed-in customer cancels their own; staff any, with the subscriptions:manage permission. Nothing is refunded (a period's refund is order.refund). It can be undone until the period ends (subscription.resume). Asked of the payment provider: the subscription shows it once the provider confirms. Staff can instead end it at once (`now: true`): nothing more is charged, nothing is refunded and what it gives stops when the provider confirms; a customer cannot. A person decides, not an AI assistant.

operations.name: subscription.change
operations.description: Move a subscription to another plan of the same kind (a membership from 3 a week to unlimited). A dearer plan is an upgrade: it takes effect now, and the payment provider charges the rest of the current period at once, prorated; the new plan applies only once that charge is paid, so nothing is given that was not paid for. A cheaper (or same-priced) plan is a downgrade: nothing is refunded or prorated, the member keeps the current plan until its period ends, and the new price is charged from the next period. What the subscription grants (a membership's classes) follows the plan when it takes effect. Only an active subscription not set to end, with no other change waiting. A signed-in customer changes their own, to a plan on sale; staff any, with subscriptions:manage. Asked of the payment provider: the subscription shows the change once the provider confirms it. A person decides, not an AI assistant.

operations.name: subscription.start
operations.description: Start a subscription to a plan (a record of an object sold every week, month or year), as a signed-in customer, a guest (with an email address) or staff for someone. Opens the payment provider's own page, which takes the card; the provider charges each period on its own schedule, after the plan's free trial when it has one. A trial is one per person per plan, and only for a signed-in customer (or staff with subscriptions:manage starting it for a person): a guest is charged from the start, and `noTrial` says why no trial was given. Starting again while the page you opened with a trial is still open gives that page. A signed-in customer with a continuation offer (moving their subscription from another platform) takes it with `offerId`: free until their paid-up date, then charged, with no trial on top; with under 48 hours left it is charged at once. Nobody starts one without the agreements the business needs for the plan (its terms, a waiver): refused with rule agreements_due and the documents while any is due, a continuation offer included (a guest passes their acceptances in `agreements`; a signed-in customer agrees first; staff send a link or record paper). The host prices it from the plan: no price is sent. Coming back to `returnUrl` changes nothing: the subscription exists once the provider confirms it. Returns the page's address and what will be charged, in minor units.

A signed-in customer agrees first (me.agreements.accept); staff never agree for anyone.

Null otherwise

operations.name: x.bookings.book
operations.description: Book the signed-in member into a class with what they already hold (a membership or a pass): the host spends one use of the one whose use would lapse first, or of `holderId` when they name one. No money moves. When the class is full they join its waitlist (unless `waitlist` is false): that spends nothing, and if a place frees before the class type's cut-off the host moves the first waiter in and spends their use then. Asked again by a member already waiting, it books them if a place is free to them (never one held for the queue), else says where they stand. Answers booked, waiting (with their position), or refused with the reason the host gave: booking not open yet (with when it opens), closed, booked by the gym only, nothing to pay with, already booked or waiting, full, or too close to the start to wait. A parent books a child the gym linked to them with forPersonId (see family): the same rules, and the child's own membership or pass pays. (Extension tool from Bookings 0.1.0.)

forPersonId.description: A child of theirs to book for instead (a dependant the gym linked to them; see family). The child's own membership or pass pays, never the parent's.

holderId.description: A membership or pass of theirs to spend, when they hold several

reason.description: no_drop_in: the class cannot be paid for online (no drop-in price). ask_desk: the address given cannot be used. try_later: too many places are held for payment just now. waitlist_closed: the class is full and it is too close to the start to wait for a place (nobody is moved in from the waitlist then). not_open: booking has not opened yet (see opensAt). closed: booking has closed. not_running: the class was cancelled or is over. person_exists: someone on file has that email (see people). possible_duplicates: people on file may be this person (see people; book one of them, or ask again with confirmNew). staff_only: this class is booked by the gym. no_use: nothing the member holds can pay for it (see detail). already_booked: they already have a place. full: no places left. too_late: the class has started, so it cannot be cancelled. not_found: no such class or booking of theirs. changed: it changed meanwhile; try again.

operations.name: x.bookings.buy
operations.description: Pay for one class (a drop-in), on the website: for a visitor, or a member with nothing to spend on it. The host makes the booking held while it is paid for (a place kept), prices it from the class's drop-in price, and starts its order; nothing is paid here. The buyer then calls order.checkout with the order's id (and a guest's token) to pay on the provider's page: the verified payment books them; an order left unpaid expires after a few minutes and the place goes back. The same rules as booking hold (when booking opens and closes, booked by the gym only, one booking per person per class); a full class is refused (only members with a membership or pass wait for a place). A signed-in member buys as themselves, or for a child the gym linked to them (forPersonId; they pay, it is the child's booking); a guest gives their email address. Cancelled in time, or by the gym, the money goes back to the card once a member of staff approves the refund; cancelled late, it is kept. Amounts in the currency's minor unit. (Extension tool from Bookings 0.1.0.)

operations.name: x.bookings.cancel
operations.description: Cancel one of the signed-in member's bookings. First without `confirm`: the host says whether a cancel now is in time (`cancelled`, the class's use given back) or late (`late_cancelled`, the use kept), by its clock. Then with `confirm: true` and `expect` set to that answer: cancelled as said, or refused if it has become late meanwhile, so a member never loses a use they were told they would keep. After the class starts it cannot be cancelled. (Extension tool from Bookings 0.1.0.)

expect.description: What the preview said; with confirm, cancel only into this state

late.description: A late cancel keeps the use the booking spent

dropIn.description: Paid for on its own: in time, the money goes back once staff approve it

operations.name: x.content.categories

operations.name: x.courses.buy
operations.description: Start an order for one course or one bundle. A signed-in customer buys as themselves; a guest gives their email address. The host prices it from the record and refuses one outside its sale window. A course the caller already holds access to is refused as one that does not exist. Nothing is paid here: the buyer then calls order.checkout with the order's id (and a guest's token) to pay on the provider's page. Amounts in the minor unit. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

agreements.description: A guest only: their acceptances of what is due, passed on to the host as they are (each { versionId, typedName, signature?, answers? }); the host checks and records them. A signed-in member agrees first.

operations.name: x.courses.catalogue
operations.description: The published courses, bundles and themes, for a catalogue page: each course's title, theme, level, summary, cover, trailer, price and number of lessons; each bundle's courses and price; the themes in their order. Prices are in the major unit of `currency`. Filter by theme or level. Only what the public may read: a draft is not here. Read-only. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

currency.description: The currency prices are in (ISO 4217), the deployment's one; null until it is set

operations.name: x.courses.course
operations.description: One published course by its address (slug): its fields, its description, its outline's sections and lessons (title, kind, minutes, whether a free preview) and, for a signed-in customer, whether they hold access and which lessons they have done. Not found for a draft or an unknown address. Read-only. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

currency.description: The currency prices are in (ISO 4217), the deployment's one; null until it is set

holds.description: The caller holds access: show open, not buy

done.description: The lesson keys the caller has done

operations.name: x.courses.lesson
operations.description: One lesson of a published course for someone who holds access to it (or any lesson marked a free preview): its kind and its material (a video and notes, a page of text, a training session, a download), where the student left its video, and the next lesson. A video is named with where it is shown: the app asks media.play for a token to play it. Not found without access, as a lesson that does not exist. Read-only. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

continueWith.description: The first lesson not done yet

operations.description: The course plans on offer: a subscription to every published course, paid every month. Each plan's title, description, price per month (in the major unit of `currency`) and the days of its free trial. Whether a person gets the trial is the host's, when they subscribe (subscription.start): one per person, signed in. Read-only. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

price.description: Per month, in the major unit of `currency`

currency.description: The currency prices are in (ISO 4217), the deployment's one; null until it is set

operations.name: x.courses.progress
operations.description: Mark a lesson started or done, and keep where its video was left (seconds), for the signed-in student. A video watched to within 10 seconds of its end counts as done (give its `duration`). The host refuses it, as a course that does not exist, when the student does not hold access to the course. Returns the lesson's progress and the course's. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

operations.name: x.courses.startSession
operations.description: For a session lesson: the signed-in student's own Programs session for it, once the program is assigned to them (it is, from the day they first open the course: the dates are a suggested pace). They then log sets with Programs' own tools. `preparing` while the assignment is being made. Not found without access to the course. (Extension tool from Courses 0.1.0.)

operations.name: x.memberships.buy
operations.description: Start an order for one pass (a class pack, a drop-in or an intro offer). A signed-in customer buys as themselves; a guest gives their email address, and may not buy an intro offer (the host refuses it: one per person, signed in). The host prices it from the pass type, refuses one not on sale, and refuses a second intro offer for the same person. Nothing is paid here: the buyer then calls order.checkout with the order's id (and a guest's token) to pay on the provider's page; the pass is granted when the provider confirms the payment. Amounts in the minor unit. (Extension tool from Memberships 0.1.0.)

agreements.description: A guest only: their acceptances of what is due, passed on to the host as they are (each { versionId, typedName, signature?, answers? }); the host checks and records them. A signed-in member agrees first.

token.description: A guest's key to this order, shown once

exerciseName.description: The exercise's name, as it was when logged

operations.name: x.programs.logAdd
operations.description: Log one set done on a session: the item (A1), the exercise when the item has more than one, the level taken when it has levels, which set (1, 2, …), what was done (reps, seconds, load) and how hard it felt (RPE). The target is taken from the session's plan, and who recorded it is the caller. A member logs on their own sessions and their class types'; a coach logs for a client (on a class session, naming them). Nobody logs on a session that is not theirs. Returns the set. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

rpe.description: How hard it felt, 1 to 10 in halves

personId.description: Staff: the person. A member is always themselves.

exerciseName.description: The exercise's name, as it was when logged

exerciseName.description: The exercise's name, as it was when logged

personId.description: Staff: the person. A member is always themselves.

plan.description: The session of the layout: blocks, items, levels and typed sets

operations.name: x.programs.sessionGet
operations.description: One session: its plan, the bank exercises it uses with the person's last numbers at each, and the sets logged on it so far. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

last.description: The sets of the last time this person did it, before this session

exerciseName.description: The exercise's name, as it was when logged

operations.name: x.programs.today
operations.description: A person's own sessions on a date (default today, UTC: pass the person's local date), each with its plan (blocks, items, levels and typed targets), the bank exercises it uses and the numbers of the last time they did each. A member sees their own; staff name the person. A class type's sessions are programs.classToday. Read-only. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

personId.description: Staff: the person. A member is always themselves.

plan.description: The session of the layout: blocks, items, levels and typed sets

last.description: The sets of the last time this person did it, before this session

operations.name: x.ticketing.eventsOnSale
operations.description: The events on sale now, soonest first, each with its ticket types (name, price and its currency, sale window, most per order, deposit) and whether places are left. Prices and deposits are in the major unit of `currency` (45.5 is 45.50). For an event page or a list of events. Only what the public may read: an event that is not on sale is not here. Read-only. (Extension tool from Ticketing 0.1.0.)

timeZone.description: The event's IANA time zone, e.g. Asia/Bangkok: show its start and end, and count its days, in this zone. Null only for an event made before events had one.

available.description: Places left, when the type says so

currency.description: The currency the prices are in (ISO 4217): the deployment's one currency, from the host. Null until an admin sets it, and until then nothing can be bought.

available.description: Places left, when the type says so

operations.name: x.ticketing.myTickets
operations.description: The signed-in customer's own tickets: each with its event (id, name, start, end, venue and state, as they are now, whether or not the event is still on sale), its ticket type (id and name), its code and its state (valid, used or void). Only the caller's tickets exist here; a code that is not theirs finds nothing. Filter by event or by code. Read-only. (Extension tool from Ticketing 0.1.0.)

code.description: Only the ticket with this code

timeZone.description: The event's IANA time zone, e.g. Asia/Bangkok: show its start and end, and count its days, in this zone. Null only for an event made before events had one.

eventStatus.description: The event's state now: draft, on_sale, ended or cancelled

operations.name: x.ticketing.orderStart
operations.description: Start an order for tickets: one or more ticket types and how many of each, paid in full or by deposit when every ticket type offers one. A signed-in customer buys as themselves; a guest gives their email address. The host prices the order from the ticket types, refuses a ticket type outside its sale window, over its most per order or without enough places left (with details naming the rule), and holds the places while the order is unpaid. Nothing is paid here: the buyer then calls order.checkout with the order's id (and a guest's token) to pay on the provider's page. Amounts are in the minor unit. (Extension tool from Ticketing 0.1.0.)

email.description: A guest's email address. A signed-in customer passes none.

agreements.description: A guest only: their acceptances of what is due, passed on to the host as they are (each { versionId, typedName, signature?, answers? }); the host checks and records them. A signed-in member agrees first.

token.description: A guest's key to this order, shown once (order.checkout and order.view take it)
